title: A broader count distribution improved held-out synaptic contact predictions in one selected MICrONS mouse
abstract: We tested contact counts for 275,986 selected MICrONS neuron pairs. Five test folds held out whole target neurons. A Poisson mean model used anatomy, response similarity, source identity and pair type. A negative binomial distribution used the same means. Its mean test log score was higher by 0.001352 natural-log units per pair. A fixed-prediction source bootstrap gave a 95 percent interval of 0.001036 to 0.001673. There were 680 pairs with two or more contacts. Poisson predicted 326.0; the broader distribution predicted 686.0. Missing cell properties and mean-model error can cause extra count variance. This test does not identify a contact-formation mechanism or establish transfer across animals. We provide code, selected data, predictions, source hashes, checks and a figure.

display.caption: Held-out contact counts and log scores in five target-disjoint folds. Both distributions use the same mean. The source bootstrap holds fitted predictions fixed.

citations.reason: Prior contact multiplicity slope; this study tests held-out count distributions.
Prior binary-mean Poisson estimator does not assert a Poisson count variance.
Prior dispersion test used homologous pairs in other species and multiple animals.
